requirements.text: initiate a high-priority case under Talent Management, account PIP-JM-2025 with description performance improvement plan to monitor his progress, assign case to HR Service Desk
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_case WHERE hr_case_id = 61 AND opened_for = 13 AND opened_by = 39 AND priority = 'high' AND coe_type = 'Talent Management' AND account_number IN ('PIP-JM-2025', 'PIP‑JM‑2025') AND short_description LIKE '%performance improvement plan%' AND short_description LIKE '%progress%' AND assignment_group = 4
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence
Jonathan Martinez is user 13, whose HR profile is 13; opened_for references hr_profile; the other Martinez users are Randy and Zachary
opened_by is the requester by the policy's case registration rule: Karen Watkins, HR profile 39
'under Talent Management' read as coe_type 'Talent Management', a value the seed uses
HR Service Desk is group 4
the request spells the account with non-breaking hyphens (U+2011); both that spelling and the plain-hyphen one are accepted
description tested by its content words, since the policy's short-description template may wrap it

disagreement: account_number: A IN ('PIP-JM-2025', 'PIP‑JM‑2025'), B 'PIP-JM-2025'; chose both spellings because the request writes the account with non-breaking hyphens (U+2011), which look the same as plain hyphens, so an agent that copies the request exactly is as faithful as one that types plain hyphens

disagreement: short_description: A LIKE '%performance improvement plan%' and LIKE '%progress%', B LIKE '%performance improvement plan%' only; chose both predicates because each is a content word of the request's description ('performance improvement plan to monitor his progress') and the tighter test still admits the policy's template

requirements.text: we need add Request Background Check service to the main case

requirements.text: ensure the case is marked as ready once all above requirements are in place
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_case WHERE hr_case_id = 61 AND status = 'ready'

id assumed next in sequence

Verify Case Creation & User Link.evidence: the request writes the account as PIP‑JM‑2025 with non-breaking hyphens (U+2011); an agent that copies it exactly fails the check's plain-hyphen equality, so both spellings are accepted; the check's other cells (Jonathan's profile, high priority, status ready) are carried unchanged

notes:
disagreement: value: the case's account_number: one pass accepts both the plain-hyphen and the non-breaking-hyphen spelling, the other only the plain one; chose both because the request itself writes the account with non-breaking hyphens (resolved on that requirement).
disagreement: value: the case's short_description: one pass tests 'performance improvement plan' and 'progress', the other only the first; kept the tighter test, since both phrases come from the request's description (resolved on that requirement).
disagreement: disposition: Verify Case Creation & User Link: one pass repaired it to accept both spellings of the account, the other kept it as written; repaired because the request's own spelling of the account uses non-breaking hyphens, which the check's plain-hyphen equality rejects.
The two passes otherwise agree on every requirement, row, id and cell, and on the other five dispositions (kept).
The acting user, Karen Watkins, holds the admin role, which the policy says must not perform routine HR case work; the request and every benchmark check expect the work done, so the requirements follow the request.
The checks that reach the case through account_number (checklist, task, knowledge link) are carried through the case id instead.
Every notification in the seed is addressed to the recipient's HR-profile personal address (Jonathan's is jonathan.martinez.13@personal.example.com); the reminder's work address is kept from the benchmark check, so an agent that uses the personal address fails that requirement.
The policy asks that cases and tasks be assigned to an active user in the group; the request assigns both to groups only and names no user, and each group has more than one active member, so assigned_to is left untested.
The policy's short-description template and 30-120 character limit are not tested by the benchmark and are left out.
Source, account_type, the checklist items' checked flags and the task's and notification's status are not fixed by the request or policy and are left untested.
